glance_takeaway: This page is a guided tour of diffusion models — how AI image generators work. The main message: every AI-generated image begins as pure random noise, and a trained network turns it into a new image through many small learned denoising steps — no existing photo is edited and no database is searched (image-to-image, where you supply a photo, is an explicit opt-in). The variants mentioned — DDIM, latent diffusion, CFG, flow matching — mostly exist to reduce ~1000 steps down to 1-4.

F1.note: Slide 2 'The forward process is fixed — no learning. Gaussian noise is added over ~1000 small steps' + slide 4 'Start from fresh random noise; denoise step by step' + slide 1 cover.

F2.note: Slide 2: '~1000 tiny additions of Gaussian noise', 'A preset noise schedule sets how much each step adds', 'Step 1000: statistically pure static'.

F3.note: Inputs (noisy image + t = 700, prompt on slide 9) and the noise target are conveyed on slide 3, but slide 3 frames noise-guessing as the network's 'one skill'; score (slide 7) and velocity (slide 11) each appear in isolation and the page never states the three are interconvertible parameterizations of the same target — a reader learns only the epsilon story.

F4.note: Slide 3: 'Training: billions of guess-the-added-noise quizzes, scored by mean-squared error. That stability — no adversarial GAN game — is why diffusion won'; slide 5 adds 'Training touches one noise level at a time'.

F5.note: Slide 5: '~1000 sequential full-network passes per image', 'every pass consumes the previous one's output — nothing runs in parallel', 'Every variant below asks: fewer steps, how?'

F6.note: Slide 6: 'The same trained network admits a deterministic sampler that tolerates big jumps: 20-50 steps instead of 1000, with modest quality loss.'

F7.note: Slide 6: 'Fixed starting noise → identical image every time — enabling inversion and interpolation.'

F8.note: Slide 7: reverse-time SDE (random walk) vs probability-flow ODE diagram, 'DDIM ≈ one discretization', 'Purpose-built ODE solvers (DPM-Solver) reach good samples in ~10-20 steps — no retraining.'

F9.note: Slide 8: diffusion runs in the VAE latent, 'decode — one pass' restores full resolution, 'VAE — a separately trained encoder-decoder'.

F10.note: Slide 8: '512 × 512 × 3 / 786,432 numbers' → 'latent: 64 × 64 × 4 = 16,384', '≈48× fewer numbers at every denoising step', 'putting Stable-Diffusion-class models on consumer GPUs'.

F11.note: Slide 9: formula 'guided = unconditional + s × (conditional − unconditional)', 'one network — prompt dropped ~10-20% of training', '2 network passes per step', 'doubles per-step cost'.

F12.note: Slide 9: 'scale s (≈7.5 default). Higher s: stronger adherence, less diversity; past ~12-15, oversaturated artifacts.' (s = 1 = no guidance is omitted, but the tradeoff and both anchor numbers land.)

F13.note: Slide 10: '1-4 steps, after retraining the model to take big jumps', progressive distillation 1000→500→…→4, 'consistency: any point ↦ the same endpoint', 'Outputs: slightly softer, less varied'.

F14.note: Slide 11: 'regression target: a constant velocity (image − noise)', 'rectified flow — a straight line', 'Straight paths need fewer steps', 'It reframes diffusion rather than rivaling it — SD3 and Flux train this way.'

F15.note: Slide 1: 'no photo edited, no database searched (image-to-image modes, where you supply one, are explicit opt-ins)'; slide 4: 'Weights encode statistics, not copies; only images repeated many times in training risk rare near-duplication — exceptional, not the mechanism.'

strengths: Near-complete factual coverage: 14 of 15 facts land verbatim-checkably, including the hard ones (F8 SDE/ODE unification, F11 CFG formula with dropout rate, F15 misconception debunk with the memorization exception).

Honest, purposeful SVG diagrams with consistent color semantics (blue = generation, red = destruction, gold = guidance, green = latent/compression) reused across slides; the latent-diffusion size comparison and the DDPM-vs-DDIM two-rail diagram encode the actual quantities.

Strong wayfinding for a scroll deck: fixed dot rail with per-slide tooltips, slide counter, numbered kickers grouping slides into mechanism/bottleneck/fixes, and a recap slide whose five lines link back to the relevant slides.
Caveats consistently carried: DDIM 'modest quality loss', latent 'slight compression-quality cost', distillation 'slightly softer, less varied', CFG oversaturation past ~12-15.
weaknesses: The glance (cover) compresses T2 into 'cut ~1000 steps to 1-4' and only name-drops latent diffusion and CFG, so T3 and T4 do not land above the fold; listing CFG among variants that 'exist to cut steps' is loose (CFG doubles cost and exists for steering, as the page itself later says).
The three interconvertible output parameterizations (noise/score/velocity, F3) are never unified; 'score' is used on slide 7 without ever being defined for a non-ML reader.
Slide 7 (SDE/ODE) is the terse outlier for the stated audience — 'probability-flow ODE' and 'the learned score' get one line each.
Recap bar chart introduces an unsourced 'rectified flow ~20-30 (fewer viable)' tier and the cover's four-line body paragraph is dense for a title slide.
Mandatory scroll-snap on desktop can fight readers who want to compare two slides.
